findings.text: In Psa 1:2, Psa 63:6, Psa 119:97 and Psa 143:5 meditation is a murmured dwelling on God, his law and his works, done by day and night and in the night watches; it is the person's own and continual.

parts.grounds: meditates day and night

findings.text: In Psa 77:12, Psa 119:15, Psa 119:23, Psa 119:27, Psa 119:48, Psa 119:78, Psa 119:148 and Psa 145:5 the meditating is a resolve, I will meditate, set on God's precepts, statutes, promise, works and deeds.

parts.grounds: I will meditate on your precepts

findings.text: In Jos 1:8 the meditating is commanded: the Book of the Law is to be meditated on day and night instead of leaving the mouth.

parts.grounds: you shall meditate on it day and night

findings.text: In Jos 1:8 the meditating leads on in a chain: it is so that the person keeps to doing what is written, and then the way is made prosperous.

parts.grounds: so that you may be careful to do

findings.text: What the devout meditation is set on, where a verse names it: the Book of the Law and God's law, precepts, statutes, testimonies and promise, his works, deeds and the splendor of his majesty, and God himself in Psa 63:6. Verses: Jos 1:8, Psa 1:2, Psa 63:6, Psa 77:12, Psa 119:15, Psa 119:23, Psa 119:27, Psa 119:48, Psa 119:78, Psa 119:97, Psa 119:99, Psa 119:148, Psa 143:5, Psa 145:5.

parts.grounds: meditate on your mighty deeds

findings.text: In Psa 1:2, Psa 119:48 and Psa 119:97 the meditation is a pursuit of its object: delight in the law and love of the commandments come just before the meditating on them.

parts.grounds: Oh how I love your law

findings.text: In Psa 63:6, Psa 77:3, Psa 77:6 and Psa 143:5 remembering comes first and meditating follows: of God, of a song in the night, of the days of old.

parts.grounds: I remember the days of old; I meditate

findings.text: The meditating is set in the night in Psa 63:6, Psa 77:6 and Psa 119:148: on the bed, in the night, in the watches of the night with the eyes awake.

parts.grounds: in the watches of the night

findings.text: In Psa 119:23 and Psa 119:78 the meditating goes on against opponents: princes plot against the servant, the insolent wrong him with falsehood, and he meditates on the statutes and precepts.

parts.grounds: your servant will meditate on your statutes

findings.text: In Psa 77:3 and Psa 77:6 the meditating goes with distress: when the speaker meditates his spirit faints, beside his moaning; after he meditates in his heart his spirit searches.

parts.grounds: when I meditate, my spirit faints

findings.text: The heart is where the meditation and the pondering take place in Psa 19:14, Psa 49:3, Pro 15:28 and Luk 2:19: the meditation of the heart beside the words of the mouth, the heart that ponders.

parts.grounds: the meditation of my heart

findings.text: In Pro 15:28 the outward act the pondering serves is an answer: the righteous heart ponders how to answer, set against the mouth of the wicked that pours out evil.

parts.grounds: ponders how to answer

findings.text: In Psa 38:12 the same verb of meditating is set on harm: the ones who seek the speaker's life turn treachery over in thought through the whole day, beside their talk of ruin.

parts.grounds: meditate treachery all day long

findings.text: In Luk 2:19 and Act 10:19 the pondering is held within: Mary treasures the things and ponders them in her heart, and Peter ponders the vision while the Spirit speaks to him.

parts.grounds: pondering them in her heart

findings.text: In Pro 5:21 the pondering is the Lord's: he weighs all the paths of a man, whose ways are before his eyes.

parts.grounds: he ponders all his paths

findings.text: In Gen 24:63 the musing is solitary, in the open field toward evening, with no object named.

parts.grounds: went out to meditate in the field

findings.text: In 1Ki 18:27 musing is named as a withdrawn state, one of several Elijah ascribes in mockery to the god of the others: musing, a journey, sleep.

parts.grounds: Either he is musing

findings.text: In Job 15:4 the meditation before God is hindered, in the same charge as setting aside the fear of God: the act is held back, not pursued.

parts.grounds: hindering meditation before God

findings.text: In Psa 19:14 and Psa 104:34 the meditation is offered to the Lord: it is to be acceptable in his sight and pleasing to him, with the words of the mouth and the rejoicing in him.

parts.grounds: May my meditation be pleasing to him

findings.text: In Psa 119:99 the meditation is the ground of understanding: because the testimonies are his meditation, the speaker understands more than his teachers.

parts.grounds: your testimonies are my meditation
